Consensus (Yahoo quoteSummary, read 2026-11-11): Q3 revenue EUR 364.7m, 18 analysts, range 352-373m; Q3 EPS EUR 1.12 from 4 analysts, up from 0.94 seven days earlier; FY26 revenue EUR 1.368bn; Q4 EUR 410m; mean target ~$303 from 21 analysts, strong_buy. On the Q2 call (2026-08-13) the CFO said 'For YORVIPATH, we expect growth and performance consistent with prior quarters' and 'relatively stable' SKYTROFA US revenue, and said analysts 'did a pretty good job modeling out Q2'. The company stopped giving patient counts (~1,000 new US Yorvipath patients a quarter). Short interest 3.0m shares, 5.4% of float, 4.2 days (2026-10-30), down from 3.48m. Last two prints were also bmo (6-Ks at 07:50 ET on 2026-05-07 and 07:55 ET on 2026-08-13). Q1: Yorvipath EUR 197m, below the ~$253m FactSet figure a Cantor note quoted. The stock gapped -5.3%, was about flat to +3% around 13:00 and closed +4.3%. Q2: revenue ~$394m against $354m consensus (Earnings Whispers). The stock opened -3.3%, sat about -3.1/-3.5% around 13:00 and closed -3.6%. So the stock has traded against the headline beat or miss on both recent bmo prints.
view: Ascendis is a launch story: Yorvipath, the hypoparathyroidism drug, makes up ~80% of product revenue. The quarter will be judged on whether it kept adding ~EUR 45-55m a quarter. Yorvipath has gone EUR 103m, 143m, 187m, 197m, 252m from Q2'25 to Q2'26, steps of +40, +44, +10 (Q1 seasonality) and +55. My own build is Yorvipath ~EUR 290-305m (management's 'consistent with prior quarters' plus a ~1% FX help: EUR/USD averaged 1.1506 in Q3 against 1.1632 in Q2 on FRED). Add SKYTROFA ~EUR 52-57m and YUVIWEL ~EUR 12-20m (~50 enrollments a month into a 65%-reimbursed funnel after EUR 7.6m in Q2), plus a small amount of collaboration revenue. That gives EUR 365-385m against a EUR 364.7m consensus whose top estimate is 373m. So the number most likely lands in line to slightly above. But the sell side has the same management steer, and I found nothing dated after the Q2 call that moves the Yorvipath trajectory either way. No IQVIA script reads, no patient update, no preannouncement; the 6-Ks since are regulatory (CHMP positive opinion for navepegritide 10-16, COMP orphan maintenance 11-06, Kidney Week data 10-26). The BioMarin YUVIWEL patent dispute settled on 2026-08-30 (20% US royalty), so that tail is gone. The release and call will probably also cover how much the reclaimed obesity program costs and how fast the buyback runs, and those are the levers that moved the stock in September. Both recent bmo prints went against their headline: a Q1 miss closed up and a Q2 beat sold off ~3% by midday. The stock comes in after a 13% rebound with calls bid. I see no direction I can defend. Revenue is a modest beat at best, which I suspect the buy side already expects. Opex or obesity spend could weigh, and the buyback could support.

recommendation.reason: The line is Yorvipath's sequential step. The consensus of EUR 365m already sits on the trajectory management told analysts to model, and I found no dated datapoint since 2026-08-13 that the estimates miss. My bottom-up is in line to slightly above, but the last two bmo prints moved against their headline. A 13% run-up with upside skew suggests the buy side expects more than the sell-side number. No mechanism clears the bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Yorvipath at or above ~EUR 310m (a clear acceleration past +EUR 55m), together with a buyback already under way and a capped obesity budget, would make a long the right side. Yorvipath under ~EUR 280m, or an R&D step-up for TransCon semaglutide, would make a short the right side.

self_critique: The case for long: management all but promised another ~EUR 50m Yorvipath step, and the stronger dollar adds a little. My build reaches EUR 375-385m, above the top analyst estimate, and analysts underestimated Q2 by ~11%. EPS revisions turned up in the last week, a fresh buyback can soak up selling, and short interest of 5% is falling. The case for short: a 13% rebound with calls bid sets a high bar, and the same setup in Q2 sold off on a beat. Opex keeps climbing (SG&A 145 to 173m) and the obesity program now has to be funded alone. Neither side has a dated datapoint the consensus misses, so 48 is honest. One search result was a TheFly headline 'Ascendis Pharma reports Q3 EPS (EUR 1.00) vs (EUR 0.72) last year'. From the figures it is most likely the Q3 2025 report, and I did not open it.
approach_notes: Writing down what the price holds first (P2.1) and the rule that a datapoint after the last call is the only edge (P3) kept this short: nothing new had appeared since the Q2 call, so I stopped. Reading the last reactions on the hourly tape at the 13:00 horizon (P6) was the most useful single step. The open-ended source list sent me after script data that is not public for a specialty pharma like this one.
